title: Support the use case of requiring authenticate to restart/shut down etc.
line: When restarting or shutting down needs a password, Plasma now asks for it instead of ending on a frozen black screen.
explanation: plasma-shutdown ended the whole session (stopping graphical-session.target, which includes the polkit agent) and only then called logind's Reboot/PowerOff. When a polkit rule requires authentication (logind reports "challenge"), logind has no agent left to ask, so the call is denied: the session is gone, the machine doesn't restart and plasma-shutdown is left hanging. Now, once apps have closed and logind reports "challenge", plasma-shutdown takes a logind delay lock and calls Reboot/PowerOff while the session is still up, so the usual password dialog appears; on success it ends the session and releases the lock so logind proceeds, and on Cancel the logout is cancelled and the desktop stays usable.

commits.message:
plasma-shutdown: ask for authentication before ending the session

When polkit requires a password to reboot or power off, logind asked for
it only after the session and its polkit agent were gone, so it failed
and left a black screen. Now we ask before ending the session instead.

BUG: 477056

media.caption: Before: Restart with a polkit rule requiring a password. logind is called after the session (and its polkit agent) has ended, so no prompt appears and the reboot is denied, leaving no session.
After: the same Restart shows the password prompt once apps have closed, while the desktop is still running.
After: pressing Cancel cancels the logout and the desktop stays usable.
